# E01 · Meet the Abacus — TRANSCRIPT OF THE RECORDED TAKE
# This file matches public/audio/about_abacus/about_abacus.mp3 (259.47 s).
# It replaces the pre-recording draft: the take was delivered as a tighter paraphrase
# in shorter sentences, so the script was rewritten to match the audio, not the reverse.
# The audio is the source of truth. Do not edit these lines without re-recording.

# --- 1 · HOOK ---
Can your child count all the way to one hundred, but ask, what's seven plus eight?
Out come the fingers!
There's a little step missing, and this is the tool that helps.
This is an abacus.
By the end of this video, you'll know every part of it.

# --- 2 · WHAT AN ABACUS IS ---
An abacus is a counting tool.
It has colorful beads that slide up and down on rods.
People used abacuses to solve maths problems long before calculators were invented.

# --- 3 · THE OUTSIDE: FRAME, RODS, BEAM ---
Let's look at the outside first.
This outside part is called the frame.
It holds everything together.
These long lines are called rods.
Some people also call them columns.
They mean the same thing.
Right across the middle is the beam.
Some people call it the bar.

# --- 4 · THE TWO HALVES ---
The beam is very important.
It splits the abacus into two parts.
Everything above the beam is the top section.
Everything below the beam is the bottom section.
Look at the top.
Each rod has one upper bead.
Now look at the bottom.
Each rod has four lower beads.
Sometimes people call them heaven beads and earth beads.
But don't worry, upper and lower are the names we'll use.

# --- 5 · WHERE TO START ---
# NOTE: "we always start" is a false rule on a 13-rod abacus. Lines 49-51 correct it
# 60 s later. See E01_meet_the_abacus.md for the on-screen mitigation.
Now look at the rod on the far right.
This is the ones column.
This is where we always start.

# --- 6 · WHAT EACH BEAD IS WORTH ---
Each lower bead is worth one.
The upper bead is worth five.
One little bead, worth five.
That's the clever part of an abacus.
Now move one rod to the left.
Everything becomes ten times bigger.
Each lower bead is now worth ten.
The upper bead is worth fifty.
Move one more rod left.
Now each lower bead is worth one hundred.
The upper bead is worth five hundred.
Every time you move left, the value becomes ten times bigger.

# --- 7 · HOW MUCH IT HOLDS ---
So how many numbers can we make?
One rod can show any number from zero to nine.
Two rods can show zero to ninety-nine.
Three rods can show zero to nine hundred and ninety-nine.
And bigger abacuses can show even bigger numbers.

# --- 7a · BIG ABACUS, SMALL ABACUS ---
Here's something interesting.
The abacus in our app has thirteen rods.
On a big abacus like that, the ones column is in the middle.
The rods on the right are used for decimals.
But on a small abacus like this one, we simply start on the far right.

# --- 8 · THE TWO FINGERS ---
Now let's learn the finger trick.
You only need two fingers.
Your thumb and your index finger.
To add lower beads, push them up with your thumb.
To add the upper bead, pull it down with your index finger.
To subtract lower beads, push them down with your index finger.
To subtract the upper bead, push it back up with your thumb.
Just two fingers, four easy rules.
That's it.

# --- 9 · READ YOUR FIRST NUMBER ---
Let's read an abacus together.
The upper bead is down. That's five.
Three lower beads are up. That's three more.
Five plus three. Eight.

# --- 10 · YOUR TURN ---
# The recall gap is real in the take: ~3.3 s of silence at 226.7-230.0.
Your turn. What number is this showing?
It's seven. One upper bead and two lower beads.
Great job.

# --- 11 · CLOSE ---
Everything you learn today is inside our app in free mode.
Tap every bead. Move them yourself. Learn by playing.
Search for abacus kids on the Apple App Store or Google Play.
Download it free.
See you in the next video, where we'll place our very first number on the abacus.
